title: Exposure-Response Tools for Time-to-Event Models
text: ertte time--event member exposure-response (E-R) package family, alongside erglm (GLM E-R models) emaxnls (Emax / logistic-Emax models), plug erplots visualisation. wraps survival::survreg()-based parametric accelerated failure time (AFT) modelling behind tidy, consistent interface: model fitting, AIC-based distribution selection, stepwise covariate modelling, simulation.

Tested officially supported "exponential", "weibull", "lognormal", "loglogistic" – see ertte_select_distribution() choosing among AIC. ... arguments passed survival::survreg().

text: survreg object extra ertte_aft/ertte_model classes

title: Fit an exposure-response time-to-event AFT model based on survreg() — ertte_aft
text: returned object class c("ertte_aft", "ertte_model", "survreg"): survreg object, little extra metadata attached. means usual survreg methods work unchanged, without needing ertte-specific equivalent – e.g. summary(), coef(), vcov(), confint(), predict(), AIC(), BIC(), logLik(), anova() comparing nested models. ertte_predict() separate, ertte-specific alternative predict() returns survival probabilities confidence intervals tidy data frame; two complementary, competing. ertte_aft() AFT-specific sibling ertte_coxph() (yet implemented), wraps survival::coxph() semi-parametric alternative. share "ertte_model" superclass, functions need generic operations (update(), anova(), SCM family) work unchanged across either engine; functions AFT-specific logic (e.g. ertte_predict(), ertte_fun()) dispatch via "ertte_aft"/"ertte_coxph" subclass. four supported distributions log-location-scale AFT models: log(T) = mu + scale * W, mu linear predictor (intercept + covariates) W follows distribution depends dist (extreme-value "exponential"/"weibull", standard normal "lognormal", standard logistic "loglogistic") – see ertte_predict() .ertte_dist_info().

title: Fit an exposure-response time-to-event AFT model based on survreg() — ertte_aft
code: mod <- ertte_aft(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ aucss, ertte_data) mod #> Call: #> survival::survreg(formula = formula, data = data, dist = dist) #>  #> Coefficients: #>   (Intercept)         aucss  #>  4.8563375087 -0.0006407913  #>  #> Scale= 0.7164032  #>  #> Loglik(model)= -1207.3   Loglik(intercept only)= -1263.9 #> 	Chisq= 113.25 on 1 degrees of freedom, p= <2e-16  #> n= 300   # other AFT distributions are also supported mod_ln <- ertte_aft(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ aucss, ertte_data, dist = "lognormal") mod_ln #> Call: #> survival::survreg(formula = formula, data = data, dist = dist) #>  #> Coefficients: #>   (Intercept)         aucss  #>  4.4908037548 -0.0006546191  #>  #> Scale= 0.978441  #>  #> Loglik(model)= -1222.3   Loglik(intercept only)= -1271.4 #> 	Chisq= 98.21 on 1 degrees of freedom, p= <2e-16  #> n= 300

title: Fit an exposure-response time-to-event Cox PH model based on coxph() — ertte_coxph
text: returned object class c("ertte_coxph", "ertte_model", "coxph"): coxph object, little extra metadata attached. means usual coxph methods work unchanged, without needing ertte-specific equivalent – e.g. summary(), coef(), vcov(), confint(), predict(), AIC(), BIC(), logLik(), anova() comparing nested models. ertte_coxph() semi-parametric sibling ertte_aft(). Unlike ertte_aft(), dist argument: Cox PH assume parametric baseline hazard, distribution select. share "ertte_model" superclass, functions need generic operations (update(), anova(), SCM family) work across either engine; functions engine-specific logic (e.g. ertte_predict(), ertte_fun()) dispatch via "ertte_aft"/"ertte_coxph" subclass.

title: Fit an exposure-response time-to-event Cox PH model based on coxph() — ertte_coxph

Calling ertte_coxph object currently errors "applicable method".

title: Prediction function for an exposure-response TTE model — ertte_fun
text: function arguments param, data, time. param argument vector location coefficients; defaults coef(object) (fitted coefficients) supplied. data argument data frame tibble; defaults object$data (data model fitted ) supplied. time argument gives time(s) evaluate survival function; recycled data.

title: Prediction function for an exposure-response TTE model — ertte_fun
text: ertte_fun() generic, methods supported engine – see ertte_fun.ertte_aft(). Named ertte_fun() consistency companion erglm/emaxnls packages' erglm_fun()/emax_fun(), serve purpose respective model classes. ertte_aft method takes fitted AFT model input returns function evaluates survival function S(t) user-specified parameters, data, times (e.g. VPCs counterfactual simulation scenarios). returned function checks param numeric one entry per column model matrix implied data, erroring informatively rather failing cryptic "non-conformable arguments" error matrix multiplication. scale always taken fitted object, param (coefficient vector coef() never includes ).

title: Prediction function for an exposure-response TTE model — ertte_fun
code: mod <- ertte_aft(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ aucss, ertte_data) mod_fun <- ertte_fun(mod)  # no arguments: reproduces the fitted model's own survival predictions s1 <- mod_fun(time = 60)  # user modifies the parameters par2 <- coef(mod) par2["(Intercept)"] <- par2["(Intercept)"] + 1 s2 <- mod_fun(param = par2, time = 60)

title: Survival-probability predictions for exposure-response TTE models — ertte_predict
text: ertte_predict() generic, methods supported engine – see ertte_predict.ertte_aft(). ertte_aft method computes linear predictor (standard error) via predict(object, newdata, type = "linear", se.fit = TRUE), converts survival probability S(t) = 1 - F((log(t) - mu) / scale), F base distribution's CDF implied object's dist (see ertte_aft() Details). Confidence intervals Wald intervals mu (qnorm() z-score times standard error), back-transformed way – parameter uncertainty scale propagated, matching level approximation used throughout package (e.g. erglm_predict()'s equivalent companion erglm package). conf_level must single number 0 1 (inclusive); values error rather silently producing reversed NaN interval.

title: Stepwise covariate modelling for exposure-response TTE models — ertte_scm
text: Terms compared likelihood-ratio Chi-squared test (stats::anova() nested survreg fits) – unlike companion erglm package's SCM, family-dependent choice test , since survreg model's likelihood ratio test vary distribution. seed exists safety measure run--run variation order candidate terms tested within step (sample(), shuffled testing one time). Model fitting (survival::survreg()) deterministic given starting formula, seed matters (essentially measure-zero) case exact p-value tie competing candidates within step – see companion erglm package's equivalent documentation full rationale, applies unchanged . candidate term aliased (perfectly collinear) term already model, stats::anova() reports NA p-value . candidate skipped step (warning) rather selected crashing search. candidates validated front: every element must parseable formula name exactly one covariate term (e.g. "sex", "sex + dose" "formula").

title: Stepwise covariate modelling for exposure-response TTE models — ertte_scm
code: mod0 <- ertte_aft(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ aucss, ertte_data) mod1 <- ertte_scm_forward(mod0, candidates = c("sex", "dose")) ertte_scm_history(mod1) #> # A tibble: 4 × 11 #>   iteration attempt step       action term_tested model_tested   model_converged #>       <int>   <int> <chr>      <chr>  <chr>       <chr>          <lgl>           #> 1         0       0 base model NA     NA          survival::Sur… TRUE            #> 2         1       1 forward    add    ~sex        survival::Sur… TRUE            #> 3         1       2 forward    add    ~dose       survival::Sur… TRUE            #> 4         2       3 forward    add    ~dose       survival::Sur… TRUE            #> # ℹ 4 more variables: term_p_value <dbl>, model_aic <dbl>, model_bic <dbl>, #> #   model_updated <int>  mod2 <- ertte_aft(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ aucss + sex + dose, ertte_data) mod3 <- ertte_scm_backward(mod2, candidates = c("sex", "dose")) ertte_scm_history(mod3) #> # A tibble: 4 × 11 #>   iteration attempt step       action term_tested model_tested   model_converged #>       <int>   <int> <chr>      <chr>  <chr>       <chr>          <lgl>           #> 1         0       0 base model NA     NA          survival::Sur… TRUE            #> 2         1       1 backward   remove ~dose       survival::Sur… TRUE            #> 3         1       2 backward   remove ~sex        survival::Sur… TRUE            #> 4         2       3 backward   remove ~sex        survival::Sur… TRUE            #> # ℹ 4 more variables: term_p_value <dbl>, model_aic <dbl>, model_bic <dbl>, #> #   model_updated <int>

text: Coefficients sampled asymptotic sampling distribution implied vcov(object), event times drawn inverse-CDF sampling fitted AFT distribution sampled coefficient vector (see ertte_aft() Details log-location-scale representation used).
